title: Predicting Audience reactions for Morning Brew

brand.name: Morning Brew
brand.logo_note: Official Morning Brew wordmark from the Morning Brew Daily brand page, recoloured to a single colour with its own alpha mask.

tagline: Test workplace, career and money questions on a simulated Morning Brew readership, scored against Morning Brew's own published audience surveys.
note: Retrospective test: Minds rated these 6 statements on 23 November 2026, after Morning Brew had already published the official survey results. It is separate from the pre-registered public forecast ledger and its headline accuracy.
intro: Minds is a simulated audience built from published evidence about real people. Ask it the questions you would put to a reader panel, and get answers without recruiting one.

labels.question: How much do you agree with this statement?

predicted.heading: Which workplace questions would readers agree with?
predicted.lead: We asked 30 Minds built on Morning Brew readers how much they agreed with 6 workplace, career and money statements, each on a 0 to 10 scale. Then we compared the order of their mean scores with the order of the yes-shares in Morning Brew's own published audience surveys.
predicted.footnote: This is a mock forecast, run after those official results were already published. Official results are yes-shares; Minds answered on a 0 to 10 agreement scale.

outcome_source: Official yes-shares from Morning Brew Inc. Insights: Workplace Trends Survey, Q1 2025, n=2,504 (five workplace and career statements), and the Investing Study, n=1,017 Morning Brew subscribers (dining out). Official results are the share who agreed or said yes. Minds answered the same statements on a 0 to 10 agreement scale.
order: Questions are listed in official agreement order (highest yes-share first). Ties share a rank.

audience.name: Morning Brew Readers (US)
audience.question: How much do you agree with this statement? 0 to 10.
audience.description: 30 Minds modelled on US readers of Morning Brew: people who read the daily newsletter at least weekly, or are email subscribers.
audience.explainer: We built 30 Minds: simulated readers of Morning Brew. Each Mind is a complete person, with an age, a job, a news habit and a voice of their own, grounded in public sources. Together they match published statistics on who reads Morning Brew, so you can put a question in front of them the way you would a reader panel.
